thread:
lynn: Customer AcmeMaps reported ~5m of 429s during a CDN cache warmup at 09:12 UTC. They say burst credits > 0 and requests were short (mostly single-shot tile gen). Can SRE triage?

nina: cc @omar — customer is on paid plan, high priority. their account id: acct_48FJ. They attached a short request trace in the ticket.

omar: grabbing logs. Which endpoint were they hitting? generate or embeddings?

lynn: generate (text), mostly sequence of parallel curl jobs from their infra as they warmed caches: 50 concurrent workers for ~3m, then ramp down. Example header from their curl: 
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
X-Client-Id: acme-maps-warmup
User-Agent: acme-cache-warmup/1.2
```
They also included our X-Rate-Limit-* headers showing: X-Rate-Limit-Burst-Remaining: 12, X-Rate-Limit-Limit: 1500 per minute.

omar: thanks. pulling quota service traces for acct_48FJ 09:00–09:30 UTC. initial look: quota ledger shows burst balance at 12 before the spike, then we saw an immediate deduction that looks larger than expected. Might be smoothing math interacting with concurrent requests.

jess: on infra side — I can see a short queue pressure on the routing layer at 09:12:22 where many requests landed on a small GPU pool. A routing fallback triggered to smaller instances for ~40s. That increased per-request accounting because retries + partial responses counted.

paul: is this the same smoothing policy we tweaked last month (smoothing window = 15s, refill granularity 1s)? customer thinks burst should cover quick spikes.

omar: yep, smoothing window is 15s. Two things likely combined: (1) CDN warmup produced a concentrated concurrency spike that exceeded per-second smoothing bucket; (2) routing fallback caused transient retries/partial-accepts which counted against tokens. Net effect: burst credits were consumed faster than the visible X-Rate-Limit-Burst-Remaining suggested.

lynn: customer sent a short repro script. gist: 50 parallel curl POSTs in a tight loop for 180s. They have reproducer if you want run it against staging.

omar: would like the repro in staging, yes. Can someone confirm a safe staging account and time window? Also want to capture quota ledger + router logs together.

nina: I gave them staging creds (acct_stg_48FJ). They can run tonight 02:00 UTC. I'll schedule with them and be on the call.

jess: infra follow-ups: I'm creating a short patch to avoid counting partial accepted attempts as full token charge during fallback; will test in canary. Created ticket INF-4821.

paul: product note — doc clarification: add a short section explaining how burst credits interact with routing retries/fallbacks and cache-warmup patterns. Customer expectations mismatch. I'll draft.

omar: short-term mitigation for AcmeMaps: recommend reducing parallel workers to <= 20 during warmup or introduce jittered ramp (10s ramp steps). Also we can temporarily raise their per-minute limit for the warmup window. Which do they prefer?

lynn: they asked for a quick increase for a single 10-minute window. Nina — can you coordinate?

nina: will ask. If they want immediate bump I can escalate to ops to grant a one-off increase.

rate-limit-bot: [automated] quota change request received for acct_48FJ: +2000/minute for 10m window. Pending manual approval.

omar: approved the one-off in console. Monitoring the ledger now.

jess: patched canary looks good: partial-accepts aren't double-counting. Rolling to more nodes.

lynn: customer confirmed they retried their warmup with smaller concurrency and saw no 429s. They're happy with temporary bump and doc guidance.

paul: created docs PR and linked INF-4821 to the release notes.

omar: follow-ups: (1) monitor other large customers for similar patterns; (2) consider smoothing-window experiment (increase to 30s or make burst-refill adaptive) — filing follow-up RFC.

lynn: thanks all — marking resolved on the ticket, leaving the RFC to SRE/Product backlog.

nina: customer success will follow up with post-mortem summary and recommend best-practice warmup guide. :thumbsup:
